# Part VI. Strategic and Social Decisions {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note .part-overview icon=false}
## Why this part comes here

An individually sensible action can fail when everyone else is adapting too. Game theory clarifies the interdependence; behavioral game theory explains how real people reason within it. Cooperation, social learning, norms, and culture then show that payoffs include fairness, identity, relationship, and shared meaning.
:::

## Guiding questions

- What game are the participants actually playing?
- Which action is best given beliefs about the others?
- What does equilibrium clarify—and what does it leave unexplained?
- Which preferences, norms, institutions, or repeated interactions can sustain cooperation?

## Bridge to the next part

Social influence can arise without a deliberate persuader. Part VII turns to intentional influence: how authority, messages, and stories change what an audience notices, believes, values, and does.
